turns.prompt_text: I'd like to redo my website. arognes.com. I made it a while ago, and it needs updating, but I want to do it completely differently. I'm just not sure how, but I think if it's less of a resume and more of a portfolio now, I want it to be more of a graph and less of a list.
turns.response_html:
Transitioning from a linear resume to a graph-based portfolio is a great way to showcase a multi-dimensional skillset. A chronological list forces you into boxes, but a graph shows how your technical projects and side pursuits actually intersect.

The Information Architecture

In a graph portfolio, visitors don't scroll down a timeline—they explore a constellation of nodes. You can cluster your work organically:

  • The Hubs (Categories): Software Architecture, Hardware & Microcontrollers, Mechanical Design, and Personal Pursuits.
  • The Nodes (Projects): Your actual work, repositories, and concepts.
  • The Edges (Connections): This is where the graph format shines. Instead of isolating skills, you show the overlap. An "IoT Swarm Trap" node visibly connects to "Hardware/RP2040" and "Beekeeping". A "Custom ABC Notation App" links to "Web Development" and "Piano". An "OpenSCAD Winch Mechanism" bridges "Mechanical Design" and "3D Printing".

When a visitor clicks a core technology like "Rust," the graph highlights every autonomous agent or backend project utilizing it.

The Tech Stack

Since you're already conceptualizing decentralized graph structures and hypergraph metadata indexes, you can build the portfolio exactly like a personal knowledge base:

  1. The Data Layer: Drive the entire site using local Markdown text files. Each project or concept gets a file with YAML frontmatter defining its tags, links, and coordinates.
  2. The Engine: Use a front-end library like react-force-graph or D3.js to render the nodes. If you want to optimize the physics calculations for a massive node count, you could write the core layout logic in Rust and compile it to WebAssembly.
  3. Deployment: Parse the text files at build time and push the static bundle to Vercel or Google Cloud for a fast, zero-maintenance pipeline.
